title: 锦瑟
author: 李商隐
intro: Perhaps the most famous puzzle in Chinese poetry: a zither, a butterfly dream, a weeping cuckoo, pearls and jade — beautiful images whose meaning readers have argued about for a thousand years. Read it for the feeling: looking back on a life and finding it already lost.
analysis: 《锦瑟》是李商隐最有名也最难懂的诗。开头说：华美的瑟为什么偏偏有五十根弦？每一根弦都让我想起过去的年华。中间四句连用四个典故：庄子梦见自己变成蝴蝶，醒来分不清是自己梦见蝴蝶，还是蝴蝶梦见了自己；古蜀国的望帝死后化作杜鹃，日夜悲啼；传说海里的鲛人哭泣，眼泪变成珍珠；蓝田出产美玉，阳光下仿佛升起轻烟。这些画面美丽又朦胧，有梦，有悲伤，有看得见却抓不住的东西。最后两句是全诗的中心：这份感情哪里要等到今天回忆才觉得怅惘，在当时就已经迷惘了。这首诗到底写什么，有人说是悼念亡妻，有人说是爱情，有人说是回顾自己的一生，至今没有定论。读的时候不必猜谜，感受那种对逝去时光的怅惘就好。
analysisEn: “The Ornate Zither” is Li Shangyin’s most famous poem, and his most mysterious. It begins with a question: why does this beautiful zither have fifty strings? Every string, every bridge, brings back a year of his youth. The middle four lines are built from four old stories. The philosopher Zhuangzi dreamed he was a butterfly and, on waking, could not tell whether he had dreamed the butterfly or the butterfly was dreaming him. An ancient king of Shu died and became a cuckoo that cried with endless grief. In the southern sea, mermaids wept tears that turned into pearls. And the fine jade of Lantian seemed to give off a haze in the warm sun. Each image is lovely and blurred — a dream, a sorrow, something you can see but never hold. The last couplet is the heart of the poem: this feeling did not have to wait for memory to become heartbreaking; even at the time, I was already lost in it. What is the poem really about? Readers have said it mourns his wife, remembers a secret love, or looks back on his whole life — there is still no agreement. You don’t need to solve the riddle. Let the images work, and feel the ache of looking back at a time that is gone.
background: Li Shangyin (c. 813–858) was one of the great poets of the late Tang, famous for dense, beautiful and often mysterious verse. Caught between two rival court factions, he spent most of his life in minor posts. This poem stands first in his collected works, which is one reason it has been read as a look back over his whole life; it is usually dated to his last years, after the death of his wife.
pronunciation: 思华年：一般读 sī；从格律看此字应为仄声，旧读 sì，网站暂按通行读 sī。瑟 sè；柱 zhù；蓝田 lán tián；惘然 wǎng rán。
version: 采用通行本，各本基本一致。

lines.py: jǐn sè wú duān wǔ shí xián
lines.lit: The ornate zither, for no reason, has fifty strings;
lines.en: Why should this painted zither have fifty strings?

lines.py: yī xián yī zhù sī huá nián
lines.lit: each string, each bridge, makes me think of my flowering years.
lines.en: Each string, each bridge, calls back a year of my youth.

lines.py: zhuāng shēng xiǎo mèng mí hú dié
lines.lit: Master Zhuang, in a dawn dream, was lost in a butterfly;
lines.en: Zhuangzi, dreaming at dawn, lost himself in a butterfly;

lines.py: wàng dì chūn xīn tuō dù juān
lines.lit: King Wang entrusted his spring heart to the cuckoo.
lines.en: King Wang gave his longing heart to a cuckoo’s cry.

lines.py: cāng hǎi yuè míng zhū yǒu lèi
lines.lit: On the blue sea, under a bright moon, pearls have tears;
lines.en: Moon bright on the wide sea — pearls that were once tears;

lines.py: lán tián rì nuǎn yù shēng yān
lines.lit: at Lantian, in warm sun, jade gives off smoke.
lines.en: sun warm on Lantian — jade breathing out a haze.

lines.py: cǐ qíng kě dài chéng zhuī yì
lines.lit: This feeling — need it wait to become a memory?
lines.en: Did this feeling have to wait to become a memory?

lines.py: zhǐ shì dāng shí yǐ wǎng rán
lines.lit: Only, at the time, I was already lost.
lines.en: Even then, at that very moment, I was already lost.

words.note: 瑟：古代弦乐器，今天很少见。
现代汉语书面语仍用，如“无端指责”。

words.en: the movable bridge under each string
words.note: 现代汉语“柱子”的“柱”，这里是乐器零件。
书面语，现代汉语说“青春年华”。
典故“庄周梦蝶”，今天仍常用。

words.en: King Wang, legendary ruler of Shu
words.note: 传说死后化为杜鹃鸟，啼叫到出血。

words.en: Lantian, a place famous for jade

words.note: 书面语，现代汉语说“回忆”。
书面语，如“怅惘”“惘然若失”。

imagery.name: 锦瑟
imagery.zh: 瑟有五十根弦，每一根都让人想起逝去的年华，是全诗的起点。
imagery.en: Each of the zither’s fifty strings calls up a lost year: the instrument opens the door to memory.

imagery.name: 蝶
imagery.zh: 庄子梦见自己变成蝴蝶，醒来分不清谁是谁——人生如梦，美好而迷惘。
imagery.en: Zhuangzi dreamed he was a butterfly and woke unsure which he really was — life as a lovely, bewildering dream.

imagery.name: 杜鹃
imagery.zh: 望帝死后化为杜鹃，啼声哀切，象征无法放下的深情和悲伤。
imagery.en: King Wang turned into a cuckoo whose cry was full of grief: a love and sorrow that cannot be let go.

imagery.name: 泪
imagery.zh: 传说南海鲛人哭泣，泪水变成珍珠；月下珠光像泪光，美丽而悲伤。
imagery.en: Legend says the tears of mermaids turned into pearls; pearls glinting under the moon look like tears.

imagery.name: 玉
imagery.zh: 蓝田的美玉在阳光下升起轻烟，看得见却抓不住，像回忆一样。
imagery.en: Jade from Lantian gives off a haze in the sun — visible but impossible to grasp, like memory.
